name: application-seat-map-selector
title: Seat Map Selector
description: Grid of seat buttons with available/taken/selected states, row labels, an aisle gap, and a legend, driven by a typed rows/seats prop contract.
useWhen: Letting users choose specific seats for a theater, flight, or event with a physical row/column layout.
Some seats must be shown as unavailable (taken) and excluded from selection.
A visual, spatial seat layout communicates position better than a plain list of seat numbers.
avoidWhen: Seating is general admission or unassigned — a simple quantity selector is enough.
The venue layout is too complex for a simple row grid (stadium sections, curved rows) — a custom SVG map may fit better.
You only need time-slot selection, not physical seats — use the Availability Grid instead.
responsiveBehavior: The seat grid is centered with fixed-size seat buttons; on narrow viewports allow the grid to scroll horizontally rather than shrinking seat buttons below a legible tap target size.
accessibility: Each seat button carries a composed aria-label naming the row, seat number, and current state (available/taken/selected).
Taken seats are real disabled buttons, not just visually dimmed clickable elements, so they're correctly skipped in keyboard navigation.
Selected seats use aria-pressed in addition to their filled background, and the legend restates all three states with both a swatch and a text label.

variants.title: Seat Map Selector
variants.description: Row-labeled seat grid with an aisle gap between seat pairs, available/taken/selected seat states, and a bottom legend.
accessibility: Taken seats are disabled buttons; available and selected states are distinguished by both fill and text label, not color alone.

variants.title: Seat Map Selector (Dark)
variants.description: Seat map grid adapted for dark surfaces with the same row-label, aisle-gap, and seat-state structure.
accessibility: Seat state fill colors and legend swatches must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
